$comment: Machine-readable brand/data policy for the ZavaGas Propane Demo Lab (issue #27). This is the single source of truth for the allowlist/denylist/exclusions used by scripts/audit-brand-policy.ps1. See docs/BRAND-POLICY.md for the human-readable explanation. The canonical fictional partner/site catalog lives in a separate single file (referenced below, not duplicated here): tools/mission-control/data/partner-catalog.json.
disclaimer: ZavaGas and all companies, people, locations, operational data, and incidents in this lab are fictional and used only for demonstration.
allowlistNotes: Contoso, Fabrikam, Adventure Works, Northwind Traders, Wide World Importers, Tailspin Toys, Fourth Coffee, and Woodgrove are well-known FICTIONAL Microsoft sample/demo brands (see docs/BRAND-POLICY.md for source links). They are allowlisted here because they are the approved canonical fictional partner catalog for this lab, not because they are real ZavaGas partners or real companies.
denylistNotes: 'Giant Pottstown' (not the bare common word 'giant') is denylisted to avoid false positives on ordinary English usage of 'giant' elsewhere in the repo, while still catching the specific real Giant Food Stores + Pottstown, PA reference named in issue #27's evidence section. Apostrophe-free variants like 'Lowes' and 'BJs' are intentionally NOT separately denylisted: they collide with ordinary camelCase code identifiers (e.g. 'BJs' matches inside 'jobJson'), so only the apostrophe forms actually used in this repo's historical content ('Lowe's', 'BJ's') are checked. All other denylist terms are specific enough (proper nouns / multi-word phrases) not to collide with ordinary prose or code identifiers.

exclusions.reason: Git internal object store and history. Immutable and out of scope for a non-destructive rebrand; git history is never rewritten.
This policy file itself must legitimately contain every denylisted term in order to check for it.
The human-readable policy document legitimately quotes the denylist terms it documents.
The audit tool's own source may reference denylist term examples in comments/tests.
Pester fixtures intentionally inject banned terms to verify the audit tool flags them (positive test cases).
Negative-case Pester fixture. Intentionally contains banned real-brand/retailer terms so the audit tool can be tested against known-bad content.

This test intentionally quotes denylisted retailer/location terms as literal negative-check strings, asserting they do NOT appear elsewhere in the deployed manifest (a regression guard, not banned content).
This test's comments reference the pre-migration 'amerigas-propane-demo' tag value only to document and verify tag-migration determinism (a regression guard, not banned content).
Binary image files are not scanned for text content (see also the media/menu.png follow-up noted in docs/BRAND-POLICY.md).
Binary image files are not scanned for text content.
Binary archive files are not scanned for text content.
Binary image files are not scanned for text content.
Dependency lockfile metadata is generated by npm and out of scope for brand content review.
Third-party dependency source code is not repository-owned content and is not tracked by git.
